title: 7-round AES-192: Impossible differential, b enumeration

target.description: Standard AES-192 under the paper's round numbering: initial whitening k0, rounds1 onward; last MixColumns omitted for 7-round recovery variants. Eight whitening bytes1,2,6,7,8,11,12,13 and k7 byte3:72 bits of named subkey material. These are selected round-key values, not an independently priced complete192-bit master key.

setting.key_relation: Two unknown AES-192 master keys K and K'=K XOR Delta, where Delta[0]=Delta[8]=a!=0 and the other22 bytes are0. Initial whitening is k0; round subkeys are k1,... .
setting.key_population: General unknown key pair with attacker-chosen nonzero a; b,c are actual key-dependent S-box output differences, not independently chosen subkeys.
setting.plaintext_model: Reuse the same two pools of2^51 plaintexts for127 feasible b hypotheses, approximated by2^7 repetitions.
assumptions: The source models pair filters and incorrect whitening-key eliminations probabilistically; those independence assumptions have not been proved for every AES key.
Named subkey bits may be dependent. No complete192-bit master-key recovery budget is supplied.
The source uses64 memory accesses per encryption equivalent; this is an accounting convention, not an independent implementation measurement.
a is chosen; b is enumerated over its127 feasible S-box differences, and c is not needed. Data and memory do not multiply by127.

success.description: The complete72-bit partial-subkey output is tested over all2^8 terminal guesses and127 feasible b hypotheses. Applying the source wrong-whitening survival model in every trial yields E_model W <= 127*2^72 exp(-64), not the per-list expectation alone. The actual b trial preserves the true output; cross-trial independence is not needed by the final first-moment step. Existing2^52 queries,2^80 processing time and2^69 bytes are retained. The existing per-bin versus aggregate pair-count conflict is not resolved; the bound is conditional on the source subsequent aggregate-count interpretation. Derived first-moment lower bound within the source random-filter model for a unique correct complete stated partial-subkey output. It is not an author-printed aggregate percentage, an experimental rate, or a proved actual-AES success probability; no full master-key recovery is asserted. Correct-tuple retention plus P_model(W>=1)<=E_model W supplies the implication without independence between different wrong tuples or auxiliary trials. The repeated-filter uniformity/independence assumptions are inherited from the source; the source also substitutes mean retained-pair counts for random counts, which is not justified as an actual-cipher upper bound by this audit.

field_conflicts.label: Per-bin versus aggregate pair count
field_conflicts.description: Section4.2 says2^-24*m^2 pairs remain in each bin after a24-bit hash. Under its uniform model this is the aggregate matching count over all bins; one specified bin has expected m^2/2^48 pairs. The subsequent2^-32*m^2 calculation uses the aggregate interpretation.
